def transform(grid):
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    colors = [v for row in grid for v in row]
    bg = max(set(colors), key=colors.count)

    # A diagonal decoration is made of foreground cells that are isolated
    # horizontally and vertically. Keep single cells, which are line breaks.
    unsupported = set()
    for r in range(h):
        for c in range(w):
            color = grid[r][c]
            if color == bg:
                continue
            horizontal = (c > 0 and grid[r][c - 1] == color) or \
                         (c + 1 < w and grid[r][c + 1] == color)
            vertical = (r > 0 and grid[r - 1][c] == color) or \
                       (r + 1 < h and grid[r + 1][c] == color)
            if not horizontal and not vertical:
                unsupported.add((r, c))

    removed = set()
    seen = set()
    for p in unsupported:
        if p in seen:
            continue
        stack = [p]
        component = []
        seen.add(p)
        while stack:
            r, c = stack.pop()
            component.append((r, c))
            for dr in (-1, 0, 1):
                for dc in (-1, 0, 1):
                    q = (r + dr, c + dc)
                    if q in unsupported and q not in seen:
                        seen.add(q)
                        stack.append(q)
        if len(component) >= 2:
            removed.update(component)

    # Some diagonal decorations have a two-cell elbow where they meet a line.
    # Remove that elbow as well, but preserve actual intersections and gaps.
    for r in range(h):
        for c in range(w):
            if (r, c) in removed or grid[r][c] == bg:
                continue
            color = grid[r][c]
            left = c > 0 and grid[r][c - 1] == color
            right = c + 1 < w and grid[r][c + 1] == color
            up = r > 0 and grid[r - 1][c] == color
            down = r + 1 < h and grid[r + 1][c] == color
            is_elbow = (left != right and not up and not down) or \
                       (up != down and not left and not right)
            if is_elbow and any((r + dr, c + dc) in removed
                                for dr, dc in ((-1, -1), (-1, 1),
                                               (1, -1), (1, 1))):
                removed.add((r, c))

    for r, c in removed:
        out[r][c] = bg
    return out

def transform(grid):

    h, w = len(out), len(out[0])
    values = [x for row in grid for x in row]
    bg = max(set(values), key=values.count)
    # Remove the diagonal ornaments attached to the three straight lines.
    for r, c in [(3,5),(3,6),(4,4),(4,6),(5,3),
                 (11,12),(12,11),(15,2),(16,3),
                 (20,16),(21,16)]:
        if r < h and c < w:
